subject: Planned DC migration — temporary response-window carveout & escalation runbook
messages:
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@clearline.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@clearline.com>, ops@clearline.com
Date: 2028-03-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planned DC migration — question on temporary SLA adjustments

Camila,

Quick one — we have a scheduled migration of our primary payments datacenter the weekend of Mar 28-29 (low-traffic window). We expect routine failovers but want to be explicit about expectations for vendor on-call and escalation while we run migration steps that may cause transient latency spikes and routing churn.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood tolerate a temporary P2 response window extension overnight (00:00–06:00 PT) for that maintenance window?
- What is the documented escalation path if a P1 shows sustained degradation during the migration (paging cadence, phone escalation, fallback model invocation)?

I've attached our migration outline. Please advise soonest — we need to lock operational runbooks with our SREs.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Turner
CTO, Clearline Payments

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@clearline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned DC migration — question on temporary SLA adjustments

Hi Michael — thanks for the heads-up and for the migration outline. We can support a scoped, temporary adjustment to the P2 response window but want to lock a brief, explicit carveout and an escalation runbook so service guarantees remain clear for both sides.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Window: 2028-03-28 00:00 PT -> 2028-03-29 06:00 PT (UTC conversion included in runbook); Redwood will treat P2s reported inside the window as "maintenance-adjusted" with a 4-hour response expectation (vs standard 2 hours).
- P1s: no SLA change. Any P1 triggers immediate page to the on-call engineer (phone + pager) and auto-creates an incident in JIRA INF-4123.
- Escalation path for P1: on-call -> team lead -> regional incident commander -> Redwood exec on-call. Phone numbers and 24/7 escalation contacts included in the runbook.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a quantized smaller model pool and enabling prefix-caching bypass to reduce cold-start pressure (see service-fallback-map.png).

Attachments: I've included a draft runbook and a service fallback map. Ben and Karthik — can you review the technical assumptions (paging cadence, model fallback behavior, and auto-scaling thresholds) and confirm we can implement the runbook with the necessary telemetry hooks?

If Clearline signs off, we can lock the carveout as an appendix to the SLO amendment and post a short DocuSign.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0147
--- attachments: redwood-sla-carveout-runbook-v1.pdf, service-fallback-map.png

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned DC migration — question on temporary SLA adjustments

Camila — looks good. Quick notes from infra:
- Paging cadence: page immediate on P1, 10-minute follow-up if not acknowledged, escalate to SLT on 30 minutes. We'll add automated reminders in PagerDuty.
- Model fallback: we can keep a warmed, quantized variant in a regional pool that accepts traffic in <200ms median extra latency; triggers can be tied to 95th-percentile latency > 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Telemetry: need request-id propagation and a short-lived sample of token-level latency for migration window (30s retention) to avoid long-term storage costs.

Laura/Marissa — can you confirm customer comms and whether offering a small SLA credit on verified P1s during the window is needed?

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
--- no attachments

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-16T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned DC migration — question on temporary SLA adjustments

Adding a couple technical constraints:
- Fallback invocation: prefer policy-based trigger (latency + error-rate combo) rather than manual flip. I'll add a rule: if p95 latency > 2s AND error-rate > 1% for 2 minutes, route new sessions to fallback pool and degrade non-critical background evals.
- KV cache warming: we will pre-warm keys for top-1k prefixes from your production telemetry; Clearline needs to provide the prefix sample CSV (anonymized).
- Observability: add an explicit metric tag migration.window=true so we can slice SLOs post-event.

I've opened INF-4123 to track implementation work: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Ops

Camila, Ben, Karthik — thanks for the fast turn. This plan looks reasonable. A few follow-ups from our side:
- Credits: for any verified P1s caused by Redwood during the migration (not the migration cutover itself), can we get a proportional SLA credit? Our procurement wants clarity.
- Prefix sample: Sara will send the anonymized prefix CSV by EOD Monday.
- Runbook sign-off: can you reduce the document to a 1-page "operational checklist" for our NOC to avoid paging noise?

If you can send the checklist and the final DocuSign by Mar 22 we can lock the migration schedule.

-Michael

- Credit: proportional SLA credit capped at 10% of that month’s spend for verified Redwood P1s attributable to our service during the window (excludes customer action-related cutover events).
